verdict.rationale: Alacritty officially supports Linux, macOS and Windows, with package managers and prebuilt binaries on each, and uses one TOML config format with imports. That is the core of a cross-platform, same-config terminal. However, a runtime probe found the macOS Homebrew cask disabled because the published binaries fail Gatekeeper, so macOS currently requires building from source or bypassing Gatekeeper. A Windows/WSL2 user also reported config gotchas and broken shortcuts. missing for 10: a working signed macOS binary install path, explicit documentation that one config file is portable unchanged across all three OSes, and independent confirmation of smooth identical-config use on Windows.
